summary: Steel observation tower on Goat Peak in Mount Tom State Reservation, Holyoke, Mass.; register dates it to 1928 and says it is maintained; used for recreation and hawk watching.

facts.design: About 42-foot steel-frame observation tower on four concrete bollards, with a 10-foot-square platform reached by three sets of stairs

access.note: On Mount Tom State Reservation and reached on foot by trails off Reservation Road. The state hike guide tells visitors to climb it.

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot. The New England Trail leads up to Goat Peak, 0.3 miles from the trailhead per the DCR hike guide.

events.note: Built 1928 per the register; still maintained
Platform floor replaced with fresh lumber

evidence.supports: On the north-western side of Mount Tom State Reservation, in Holyoke
evidence.quote: The Goat Peak Lookout Tower is on the north-western side of the Mount Tom State Reservation in Holyoke Massachusetts.

evidence.supports: Goat Peak rises to 822 feet and is a subsidiary peak of Mount Tom
evidence.quote: Goat Peak (822') is a subsidiary peak of Mt. Tom (1,202').
Goat Peak Lookout tower was built in 1928 and is still maintained to this day.
It is about 42' feet tall with a 15.5' base.

evidence.supports: steel frame on four concrete bollards
evidence.quote: The steel frame rests atop four concrete bollards.

evidence.supports: 10-foot-square platform reached by three sets of stairs
evidence.quote: The viewing platform is a 10' square and is reached by three sets of stairs.
The platform floor was recently replaced with fresh lumber as of 2025.

evidence.supports: used for recreational viewing and the annual fall hawk migration
evidence.quote: The tower is currently used for recreational viewing, and for witnessing the annual southern hawk migration each fall.

evidence.supports: reached by several trails branching off Reservation Road
evidence.quote: It is accessible by several trails branching off Reservation Road, which bisects the forest.

evidence.supports: hike guide calls it an observation tower with maybe the best view on the Mount Tom Range
evidence.quote: Goat Peak offers you an observation tower with maybe the best view on the Mount Tom Range

evidence.supports: hike guide tells visitors to climb it
evidence.quote: Climb the Goat Peak observation tower and enjoy the view.

evidence.supports: Goat Peak is 0.3 miles up the New England Trail
evidence.quote: Follow the NET up to Goat Peak (0.3 miles).

evidence.supports: two viewing towers, one on Goat Peak
evidence.quote: Overlooking Westhampton and beyond, as well as a second tower to the north on Goat Peak, are Mt. Tom State Reservation’s two viewing towers.

evidence.supports: second tower reached by the New England National Scenic Trail
evidence.quote: Reach of the second tower on Goat Peak is by way of the New England National Scenic Trail ( NET ).

evidence.supports: a viewing tower at the Visitor Center, reached from its parking area
evidence.quote: Access to the Visitor Center tower is via the parking area rear of the Visitor Center.

sources.title: Mount Tom State Reservation (hike guide)
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation

sources.title: Viewing Towers
sources.publisher: Exploring the Mt. Tom Range and State Reservation

notes_for_editor: The 1928 build date rests on the register page alone; no second source found. Searches surfaced a 1928 Goat Peak lookout in Washington State, a different site, so do not conflate them. Sources describe recreation and hawk watching only; none says the tower was built for fire watch, so the brief's kind 'unknown' is left as is. Current access comes from the DCR hike guide and an advocacy site. A check with the DCR Mount Tom office or MACRIS would settle the 1928 date.
